events.title: Political pushback to the NextEra-Dominion deal has spread to New England
events.summary: The proposed $67-billion merger between NextEra and Dominion Energy, which would create the world's largest regulated utility, is facing increasing political opposition beyond Virginia, spreading to New England states. Governors from Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, and Vermont have voiced concerns about the unprecedented concentration of leverage and its potential impact on regional energy markets and ratepayers. This pushback is partly fueled by NextEra's past attempts to block a major transmission line in Maine, raising questions about the deal's ultimate approval despite company assurances of a "win-win" scenario.

articles.headline: Political pushback to the NextEra-Dominion deal has spread to New England

events.title: Americans of All Incomes Head to Dollar Stores to Stay Frugal
events.summary: Dollar General and Dollar Tree have reported significant sales gains and increased store traffic, driven by shoppers seeking value amidst economic uncertainty and higher gas prices. Both companies noted that while their core customers remain financially constrained, higher-income shoppers are also increasingly visiting their stores, highlighting a broader shift towards frugality. This trend comes as other major retailers like Walmart and Target are also focusing on price reductions to attract cost-conscious consumers.

articles.headline: Americans of All Incomes Head to Dollar Stores to Stay Frugal

events.title: Resilient Alphabet C stock weathers heavy AI capex after Q2 2026 earnings beat
events.summary: Alphabet Class C stock trades in the high $330s as of late August 2026, demonstrating resilience despite negative free cash flow from aggressive AI infrastructure investments. The company reported strong Q2 2026 earnings, with revenue up 24.23% and Google Cloud revenue surging 82%, alongside an expansion in cloud operating margin. While facing a $692 billion market value reduction due to AI execution risk concerns, Alphabet has initiated a dividend and authorized an $85 billion stock issuance to finance future growth.

articles.headline: Resilient Alphabet C stock weathers heavy AI capex after Q2 2026 earnings beat

events.title: Zacks Industry Outlook PulteGroup, M/I Homes and Century
events.summary: The Zacks Building Products - Home Builders industry is poised for long-term growth in 2026 due to tight housing supply, steady demand, and easing mortgage rates, benefiting companies like PulteGroup, M/I Homes, and Century Communities. Despite near-term challenges such as affordability issues, high land costs, and reliance on sales incentives, the industry's structural housing shortage and favorable demographics support future demand. Builders are adapting through build-to-order models, community expansion, disciplined inventory management, and technology adoption to navigate these challenges and capitalize on growth opportunities.

articles.headline: Zacks Industry Outlook PulteGroup, M/I Homes and Century
